row.evidence: Sanity's pricing page lists 'Single sign-on with SAML' only on Enterprise and no SCIM on any plan; its docs say SAML user accounts 'will not be removed automatically because the IdP does not send permissions updates other than when a user logs in.'
row.notes: Unchanged status (none). SAML SSO is now Enterprise-only: the pricing page's Growth add-ons are Dedicated Support ($799/mo), Increased quota ($299/mo) and Extra datasets ($999/dataset/mo), so June's '$1,399/mo Growth SAML add-on' has no first-party source and is dropped. Growth is $15/seat/month, monthly only (self-serve plans cannot pay annually). SAML creates users on first login with group-to-role mapping; removal is manual or via the Access API. No SCIM found in the docs index, llms-full export or HTTP API reference.

plans.name: Growth
plans.notes: Self-serve plans are monthly only; up to 50 seats.

scim.notes: No SCIM endpoint in Sanity's docs, llms-full export, pricing page or HTTP API reference. SAML users are created on first login and role mapping runs at login; accounts are not removed automatically.

limitations.text: Without SCIM, users removed in the IdP keep their Sanity account until removed manually or via the Access API.

audit_log_api.notes: Activity Log API covers management activity; the pricing page lists 'Audit log: content changes and events' as Enterprise 'Custom'.

limitations.text: Role changes return 409 when role assignments are managed via SAML.

okta.notes: No Sanity app on okta.com/integrations (sanity, sanity-io both 404); Sanity's SAML guide uses Okta as its example IdP with a custom SAML app.

entra.notes: Sanity's Entra guide uses a non-gallery enterprise application; no Microsoft Learn tutorial found (sanity-tutorial 404).

jumpcloud.notes: Sanity's JumpCloud guide uses a Custom Application.

citations.title: Setting up single sign-on with SAML
citations.quote: This guide walks through creating a SAML SSO configuration for your organization, mapping identity provider groups to Sanity roles, and configuring your studio to use SAML login.

citations.title: Setting up single sign-on with SAML
citations.quote: When auto update roles on login is enabled, Sanity re-evaluates your role mapping rules every time a user logs in with SAML SSO

citations.title: Setting up single sign-on with SAML
citations.quote: Sanity matches a returning user to an existing account by the identifier in the SAML assertion — the nameID or the id attribute — combined with the SAML SSO configuration that sent it. If either changes, the next login creates a new user instead of matching the existing one.

citations.title: Setting up single sign-on with SAML
citations.quote: A SAML identity is a separate account from a user's previous Google, GitHub, or email login. Anyone who switches to SAML SSO occupies two seats until you remove their old account.

citations.title: Reconcile users against internal systems
citations.quote: SAML validates users when they log in. Users without permission to log in via your identity provider (IdP) will not have access. However, their user account will not be removed automatically because the IdP does not send permissions updates other than when a user logs in.
